container_info.description: This project aims to develop a comprehensive functional test plan for Wi-Fi 7 (IEEE 802.11be) devices, focusing on non-performance aspects. The plan will cover Multi-Link Operation (MLO) with mandatory Multi-Link Single Radio (MLSR) and optional Multi-Link Multi Radio (MLMR) scenarios, security validation for WPA2 and WPA3 protocols, and basic stability test cases. The outcome will be a structured, reusable test plan suitable for device certification, QA, and interoperability testing.
container_info.reasoning: The project is primarily a server-side test-plan and test orchestration service (documentation, APIs, automation) for Wi‑Fi device validation — clearly backend. The container already includes Python3, uvicorn and related tooling, making a lightweight ASGI Python framework the natural fit. FastAPI is modern, minimal for headless containers, has excellent typing and auto-generated docs (useful for test plans and API-driven test execution), and pairs directly with uvicorn for development. It is more suitable here than full-stack web/frontend frameworks since the work focuses on backend test orchestration, documentation generation, and automation integrations (Celery already present for task queues).
requirements: uvicorn[standard] (use existing uvicorn for ASGI dev server)
pydantic (installed as FastAPI dependency) for validation
minimal task runner: celery (already present) and kombu if needed
sqlite3 (use built-in sqlite for lightweight storage; no external DB required)
make or simple shell scripts for build/run automation (use bash)
pytest (for minimal test validation) or builtin unittest
sphinx or mkdocs (already present) only if generating documentation artifacts
basic environment variables for configuration (no production config management)
small requirements.txt or pyproject.toml listing only fastapi, uvicorn, pytest and celery-related minimal deps

steps.name: environment - global env and runtime verification
steps.description: Persist minimal global environment variables into /etc/profile.d/core_doc_hub.sh using the absolute workspace path so future shells include the workspace venv bin. Create a pinned requirements.txt only if missing. Verify presence and record versions of python3, pip, system uvicorn and celery. Use sudo tee and sudo cmp/cat for idempotent safe writes.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
PROFILE=/etc/profile.d/core_doc_hub.sh
# prepare content with WORKSPACE expanded at write-time
PROFILE_CONTENT="# CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub environment\nexport APP_ENV=development\nexport PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1\nexport PATH=\"${WORKSPACE}/.venv/bin:\$HOME/.local/bin:\$PATH\"\n"
# compare existing file content (use sudo cat) and write via sudo tee atomically if different/missing
if sudo test -f "$PROFILE"; then
  if ! sudo bash -c "cat '$PROFILE'" | cmp -s - <(printf '%s' "$PROFILE_CONTENT") 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "/etc/profile.d/core_doc_hub.sh exists and differs; leaving existing file" >&2
  fi
else
  printf '%s' "$PROFILE_CONTENT" | sudo tee "$PROFILE" >/dev/null
  sudo chmod 644 "$PROFILE"
fi
# ensure workspace exists
mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE" && cd "$WORKSPACE"
# create pinned requirements.txt only if missing
if [ ! -f "$WORKSPACE/requirements.txt" ]; then
  cat > "$WORKSPACE/requirements.txt" <<'REQ'
fastapi>=0.95,<1.0
uvicorn[standard]>=0.22,<1.0
pytest>=7.0,<8.0
celery>=5.2,<6.0
kombu>=5.2,<6.0
requests>=2.28,<3.0
REQ
fi
# collect tool versions (system and runtime)
{
  python3 --version 2>&1 || true
  python3 -m pip --version 2>&1 || true
} > "$WORKSPACE/tool_versions.txt"
# surface system uvicorn/celery if present
if command -v uvicorn >/dev/null 2>&1; then uvicorn --version 2>&1 >> "$WORKSPACE/tool_versions.txt" || true; else echo "uvicorn: absent" >> "$WORKSPACE/tool_versions.txt"; fi
if command -v celery >/dev/null 2>&1; then celery --version 2>&1 >> "$WORKSPACE/tool_versions.txt" || true; else echo "celery: absent" >> "$WORKSPACE/tool_versions.txt"; fi

steps.name: scaffolding - create FastAPI skeleton, start/stop scripts, .env, .gitignore and README
steps.description: Create a minimal FastAPI app with /health, guarded Celery tasks module (no broker connection at import time), a .env that points to sqlite:///./data.db and optional CELERY_BROKER_URL, and robust start/stop scripts that use the workspace venv python, write atomic pidfile, capture PID reliably, preserve uvicorn logs to $WORKSPACE/uvicorn.log, and include fallbacks for PID discovery (ss/netstat/lsof). All generated files expand WORKSPACE at generation time and are idempotent.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE/app" "$WORKSPACE/app/tasks" && cd "$WORKSPACE"
# app/main.py (idempotent)
if [ ! -f "$WORKSPACE/app/main.py" ]; then
  cat > "$WORKSPACE/app/main.py" <<'PY'
from fastapi import FastAPI
app = FastAPI()

@app.get('/health')
def health():
    return {'status': 'ok'}
PY
fi
# guarded celery tasks - avoid broker connection at import
if [ ! -f "$WORKSPACE/app/tasks/__init__.py" ]; then
  cat > "$WORKSPACE/app/tasks/__init__.py" <<'PY'
try:
    from celery import Celery
except Exception:
    Celery = None

def get_celery():
    if Celery is None:
        return None
    return Celery('core_doc_hub', broker='redis://localhost:6379/0')

# example task

def ping_task():
    c = get_celery()
    if c is None:
        return 'broker-unavailable'
    @c.task
    def ping():
        return 'pong'
    return ping
PY
fi
# write a small .env to use local sqlite and optional broker
if [ ! -f "$WORKSPACE/.env" ]; then
  cat > "$WORKSPACE/.env" <<ENV
DATABASE_URL=sqlite:///./data.db
# set CELERY_BROKER_URL to enable celery during dev, default left empty
CELERY_BROKER_URL=
ENV
fi
# start script: capture pid immediately, log output, write atomic pidfile
START="$WORKSPACE/start.sh"
cat > "$START" <<BASH
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="$WORKSPACE"
cd "${WORKSPACE}"
PIDFILE="$WORKSPACE/.uvicorn.pid"
LOGFILE="$WORKSPACE/uvicorn.log"
PORT=8000
PY="$WORKSPACE/.venv/bin/python"
CMD=("$PY" -m uvicorn app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port "$PORT")
# prefer venv python when available
if [ ! -x "$PY" ]; then
  PY=python3
  CMD=("$PY" -m uvicorn app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port "$PORT")
fi
# start background process and capture pid reliably
("${CMD[@]}" ) >>"$LOGFILE" 2>&1 &
PID=$!
# write pidfile atomically
TMP=
TMP=$(mktemp "${PIDFILE}.tmp.XXXX") && printf '%s' "$PID" > "$TMP" && mv "$TMP" "$PIDFILE"
# wait briefly for listener
for i in {1..20}; do
  if command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1; then ss -ltn | grep -E ":$PORT( |$)" >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; fi
  if command -v netstat >/dev/null 2>&1; then netstat -ltn | grep -E ":$PORT( |$)" >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; fi
  sleep 0.5
done
exit 0
BASH
chmod +x "$START"
# stop script: validate pidfile, attempt graceful shutdown, fallback to port-based kill
STOP="$WORKSPACE/stop.sh"
cat > "$STOP" <<'BASH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="$WORKSPACE"
PIDFILE="$WORKSPACE/.uvicorn.pid"
PORT=8000
if [ ! -f "$PIDFILE" ]; then echo "no pidfile"; exit 0; fi
PID=$(cat "$PIDFILE" 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -n "$PID" ] && ps -p "$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  kill -TERM "$PID" || true
  for i in {1..10}; do
    if ! ps -p "$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then rm -f "$PIDFILE"; exit 0; fi
    sleep 0.5
  done
  kill -KILL "$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  rm -f "$PIDFILE"
  exit 0
fi
# if pidfile invalid, attempt to find process listening on port and kill it
if command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  PIDS=$(ss -ltnp 2>/dev/null | awk -v p=":$PORT" '$0~p{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i~/pid=/){split($i,a,",");for(j in a) if(a[j]~/pid=/){split(a[j],b,/pid=|,/);print b[2]}}}') || true
else
  PIDS=$(netstat -ltnp 2>/dev/null | awk -v p=":$PORT" '$0~p{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i~/pid=/){split($i,a,",");for(j in a) if(a[j]~/pid=/){split(a[j],b,/pid=|,/);print b[2]}}}') || true
fi
if [ -n "$PIDS" ]; then
  for p in $PIDS; do kill -TERM "$p" || true; done
fi
rm -f "$PIDFILE" || true
exit 0
BASH
chmod +x "$STOP"
# .gitignore and README
if [ ! -f "$WORKSPACE/.gitignore" ]; then
  cat > "$WORKSPACE/.gitignore" <<'GIT'
.venv
.uvicorn.pid
uvicorn.log
data.db
tests/pytest.log
__pycache__/
GIT
fi
if [ ! -f "$WORKSPACE/README.md" ]; then
  cat > "$WORKSPACE/README.md" <<'RD'
# CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub

Use ./start.sh and ./stop.sh. Configure runtime via .env. Tests: ./test.sh (generated by test step).
RD
fi

steps.name: dependencies - create venv, install pinned Python deps with explicit venv tooling
steps.description: Create a workspace venv (idempotent), ensure setuptools/wheel and pip are available in the venv, install pinned requirements into the venv using fully-qualified venv pip. If venv creation fails or pip install fails, attempt python3 -m pip --user install as fallback. Record venv package versions using pip list --format=json and record tool versions. This step ensures no accidental system-wide installs.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
VENV="$WORKSPACE/.venv"
PY="$VENV/bin/python"
PIP="$VENV/bin/pip"
# create venv if missing
if [ ! -d "$VENV" ]; then
  python3 -m venv "$VENV" || { echo "venv creation failed" >&2; VENV_ERR=1; }
fi
# ensure venv pip/python references
if [ -x "$PY" ]; then
  "$PY" -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  PKG_PIP="$PIP"
  PKG_PY="$PY"
else
  echo "venv not available; will attempt user installs" >&2
  PKG_PIP="python3 -m pip"
  PKG_PY="python3"
fi
# install requirements into venv (or --user fallback)
if [ -f "requirements.txt" ]; then
  if [ -x "$PIP" ]; then
    "$PIP" install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt || INSTALL_ERR=1
  else
    python3 -m pip install --user --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt || INSTALL_ERR=1
  fi
fi
if [ "${INSTALL_ERR-0}" = "1" ]; then
  echo "install failed in venv, attempting --user fallback" >&2
  python3 -m pip install --user --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt || { echo "pip install failed in venv and --user; aborting" >&2; exit 4; }
fi
# record venv package versions using pip list --format=json
if [ -x "$PIP" ]; then
  "$PIP" list --format=json > "$WORKSPACE/venv_packages.json" || true
else
  python3 -m pip list --format=json > "$WORKSPACE/venv_packages.json" || true
fi
# record tool versions (system and venv)
{
  echo "system_python: $(python3 --version 2>&1 || true)"
  echo "system_pip: $(python3 -m pip --version 2>&1 || true)"
  if [ -x "$PY" ]; then
    echo "venv_python: $($PY --version 2>&1 || true)"
    echo "venv_pip: $($PY -m pip --version 2>&1 || true)"
  fi
} > "$WORKSPACE/tool_versions.txt"

steps.name: testing - create pytest test and run tests inside venv
steps.description: Create a minimal pytest test that uses FastAPI TestClient to hit /health. Run tests using the workspace venv python when available and capture pytest logs for diagnostics. Generate a small test summary using the same venv python to avoid environment mismatches.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE/tests"
if [ ! -f "$WORKSPACE/tests/test_health.py" ]; then
  cat > "$WORKSPACE/tests/test_health.py" <<'PY'
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_health():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r = client.get('/health')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert r.json().get('status') == 'ok'
PY
fi
PYBIN="$WORKSPACE/.venv/bin/python"
if [ -x "$PYBIN" ]; then
  "$PYBIN" -m pytest tests | tee "$WORKSPACE/tests/pytest.log" || (echo "pytest failed, see $WORKSPACE/tests/pytest.log" >&2; exit 6)
  "$PYBIN" - <<'PY' > "$WORKSPACE/tests/test_summary.txt"
import sys
print('pytest log: tests/pytest.log')
PY
else
  python3 -m pytest tests | tee "$WORKSPACE/tests/pytest.log" || (echo "pytest failed, see $WORKSPACE/tests/pytest.log" >&2; exit 6)
  python3 - <<'PY' > "$WORKSPACE/tests/test_summary.txt"
import sys
print('pytest log: tests/pytest.log')
PY
fi

steps.name: validation - build, start server, health-check (with retries), run tests, and stop
steps.description: Start the application via ./start.sh, poll for LISTEN and perform HTTP health checks with retries. If pidfile is missing or invalid, attempt to find processes listening on the port and clean them. Run pytest runtime tests using the venv python and capture runtime pytest logs. Check redis/redis-cli presence and warn if absent; skip celery-specific validations when broker is not configured. Provide diagnostics (ss/netstat, ps, tail of uvicorn.log) on failures and stop the server gracefully. Use absolute workspace paths for PID and logs.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
PIDFILE="$WORKSPACE/.uvicorn.pid"
LOGFILE="$WORKSPACE/uvicorn.log"
PORT=8000
# check redis broker presence but do not fail
if command -v redis-cli >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  if ! redis-cli -h localhost -p 6379 ping >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "warning: redis not responding; celery broker unavailable" >&2
    REDIS_OK=0
  else
    REDIS_OK=1
  fi
else
  if pgrep -f redis-server >/dev/null 2>&1; then REDIS_OK=1; else echo "warning: redis not running; celery broker unavailable" >&2; REDIS_OK=0; fi
fi
# start server
./start.sh
# wait for listen and health
OK=0
for i in {1..20}; do
  if command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1; then ss -ltn | grep -E ":$PORT( |$)" >/dev/null 2>&1 && true || true; fi
  if curl -sS -f "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then OK=1; break; fi
  sleep 0.5
done
if [ "$OK" -ne 1 ]; then
  echo "health check failed; diagnostics:" >&2
  if command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1; then ss -ltnp | sed -n '1,200p' >&2 || true; fi
  ps aux | grep -E 'uvicorn|app.main' | sed -n '1,200p' >&2 || true
  echo "--- uvicorn log (tail) ---" >&2
  tail -n 200 "$LOGFILE" 2>/dev/null || true
  # attempt cleanup: try stop script, then kill listeners on port
  ./stop.sh || true
  if command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    PIDS=$(ss -ltnp 2>/dev/null | awk -v p=":$PORT" '$0~p{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i~/pid=/){split($i,a,",");for(j in a) if(a[j]~/pid=/){split(a[j],b,/pid=|,/);print b[2]}}}') || true
  else
    PIDS=$(netstat -ltnp 2>/dev/null | awk -v p=":$PORT" '$0~p{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i~/pid=/){split($i,a,",");for(j in a) if(a[j]~/pid=/){split(a[j],b,/pid=|,/);print b[2]}}}') || true
  fi
  if [ -n "$PIDS" ]; then for p in $PIDS; do kill -TERM "$p" || true; done; fi
  exit 7
fi
# run runtime tests using venv python
PYBIN="$WORKSPACE/.venv/bin/python"
if [ -x "$PYBIN" ]; then
  "$PYBIN" -m pytest tests | tee "$WORKSPACE/tests/pytest_runtime.log" || (echo "runtime pytest failed" >&2; ./stop.sh || true; exit 8)
else
  python3 -m pytest tests | tee "$WORKSPACE/tests/pytest_runtime.log" || (echo "runtime pytest failed" >&2; ./stop.sh || true; exit 8)
fi
# stop server gracefully
./stop.sh || true
# confirm stopped or clean up remaining listeners
if [ -f "$PIDFILE" ]; then
  echo "failed to stop uvicorn (pidfile remains)" >&2
  ps -p "$(cat "$PIDFILE")" -o args= || true
  exit 9
fi
exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Validation script: build/start/healthcheck/run tests/stop using absolute workspace paths
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
PIDFILE="$WORKSPACE/.uvicorn.pid"
LOGFILE="$WORKSPACE/uvicorn.log"
PORT=8000
RETRIES=20
SLEEP_MS=0.5

# warn about redis broker availability but do not fail
REDIS_OK=0
if command -v redis-cli >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  if redis-cli -h localhost -p 6379 ping >/dev/null 2>&1; then REDIS_OK=1; else echo "warning: redis not responding; celery broker unavailable" >&2; REDIS_OK=0; fi
else
  if pgrep -f redis-server >/dev/null 2>&1; then REDIS_OK=1; else echo "warning: redis-cli/redis-server not found; celery broker unavailable" >&2; REDIS_OK=0; fi
fi

# start server
if [ ! -x "./start.sh" ]; then echo "error: ./start.sh not found or not executable" >&2; exit 2; fi
./start.sh || (echo "start.sh returned non-zero" >&2; exit 3)

# wait for LISTEN and /health
OK=0
for i in $(seq 1 "$RETRIES"); do
  # optional check for LISTEN; don't fail on missing ss/netstat
  if command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1; then ss -ltn | grep -E ":$PORT( |$)" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi
  if curl -sS -f "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then OK=1; break; fi
  sleep "$SLEEP_MS"
done

if [ "$OK" -ne 1 ]; then
  echo "health check failed; collecting diagnostics..." >&2
  if command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1; then ss -ltnp 2>/dev/null | sed -n '1,200p' >&2 || true; fi
  if command -v netstat >/dev/null 2>&1; then netstat -ltnp 2>/dev/null | sed -n '1,200p' >&2 || true; fi
  ps aux | grep -E 'uvicorn|app.main' | sed -n '1,200p' >&2 || true
  echo "--- uvicorn log (tail) ---" >&2
  tail -n 200 "$LOGFILE" 2>/dev/null || true

  # attempt graceful stop
  ./stop.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

  # find PIDs listening on port and kill
  PIDS=""
  if command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    PIDS=$(ss -ltnp 2>/dev/null | awk -v p=":$PORT" '$0~p{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i~/pid=/){split($i,a,",");for(j in a) if(a[j]~/pid=/){split(a[j],b,/pid=|,/);print b[2]}}}') || true
  elif command -v netstat >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    PIDS=$(netstat -ltnp 2>/dev/null | awk -v p=":$PORT" '$0~p{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i~/pid=/){split($i,a,",");for(j in a) if(a[j]~/pid=/){split(a[j],b,/pid=|,/);print b[2]}}}') || true
  fi
  if [ -n "$PIDS" ]; then
    for p in $PIDS; do kill -TERM "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 || kill -KILL "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; done
  fi
  exit 7
fi

# run runtime tests using venv python if available, capture logs
PYBIN="$WORKSPACE/.venv/bin/python"
mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE/tests"
if [ -x "$PYBIN" ]; then
  "$PYBIN" -m pytest tests | tee "$WORKSPACE/tests/pytest_runtime.log" || (echo "runtime pytest failed" >&2; ./stop.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; exit 8)
else
  python3 -m pytest tests | tee "$WORKSPACE/tests/pytest_runtime.log" || (echo "runtime pytest failed" >&2; ./stop.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; exit 8)
fi

# stop server gracefully
./stop.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

# confirm stopped; if pidfile remains try to report and clean
if [ -f "$PIDFILE" ]; then
  PIDVAL="$(cat "$PIDFILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  echo "failed to stop uvicorn (pidfile remains): $PIDFILE -> $PIDVAL" >&2
  if [ -n "$PIDVAL" ]; then ps -p "$PIDVAL" -o pid,cmd || true; kill -TERM "$PIDVAL" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi
  sleep 0.5
  if [ -f "$PIDFILE" ]; then rm -f "$PIDFILE" || true; fi
  exit 9
fi

exit 0
